source.title: Exploring OpenAI's Latent Directions: Tests, Observations, and Poking Around

record.file_problem: none; full post and comments are present
record.tranche_reason: Applies semantic-matching tests to SAE directions and neurons in GPT2-SMALL, a new setting for evidence about feature representations; it does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: Tests search for and semantic matching of concepts in SAE directions and neurons. It reports manual match counts and activation spot-checks, not measurements of overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, representational capacity, or feature dimensionality. Mentioned search rankings and example directions are not counted unless the post reports a result for them.
record.test_reason: The post manually compares OpenAI SAE directions with raw neurons in GPT2-small on whether they pick out single, meaningful concepts. That is indirect, exploratory evidence for V4: a dictionary recovers interpretable sparse features that neurons do not cleanly carry. It does not touch toy-model geometry, capacity, canonicity or dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes directions were consistently and significantly better than neurons at identifying concepts, but worse in later layers, and draws no conclusions about superposition geometry or capacity. The record's claim of an internal inconsistency in the layer-0 exclusion counts is wrong: the first 22/25 refers to the share of results from layer 0. There is a real inconsistency at layer 8, where the table shows directions 12 versus neurons 13 against the prose claim of 'every layer'.
record.recipe_differences: Interactive semantic search and manual inspection of GPT2-SMALL SAE directions and neurons; no toy-network superposition intervention or geometry measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer changed match counts; excluding layer 0 reduced the reported match count, and synonym activation was weaker than activation on the original token. The layer-exclusion passage reports 22/25 both before and after exclusion while also saying three fewer matches, an internal inconsistency.
record.problems: Exploratory, manually judged semantic matching; a small number of selected prompts and one text snippet; no stated uncertainty or control condition; layer-exclusion counts are internally inconsistent. The post notes that GPT2-SMALL is an older, weak token predictor, but does not conduct a capability control.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results directly measuring the claim’s other versions were extracted. Anecdotal direction examples and questions without a distinct test outcome are omitted.

untested.parts: No toy networks, no overlap or near-orthogonal geometry, no sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation of dimensions.
Polysemantic neurons are observed, but their cause is not examined.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features. Anecdotes such as the love/hate direction and cross-layer 'triplets' are not tests.
Uses 1-D directions but does not test whether features are 1-D.

missing.what: Spot-check of direction 0-MLP-OAI:19642: it activated on 'insightful' and 'intuition' but not on 'absurd', a minimal control for concept-level rather than token-level matching.

The direction-quality claim rests partly on a few hand-picked examples, such as polysemantic neuron 11:2172 and rogue directions 10-MLP-OAI:0 and 11-MLP-OAI:1, which the author infers are polysemantic.
missing.locator: It's All Greek To Me; From Hero... to Zero?

record.verdict_notes: Single-author exploratory LessWrong post. One model, one SAE, two hand-picked tests, manual match judgments, no uncertainty and essentially no controls. The evidence weight for V4 is low.

versions.untested_parts: No test of toy networks, sparse-feature overlap, near-orthogonal geometry, or sparsity-dependent transitions.
No test of capacity competition or whether importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Although the post describes some neurons as polysemantic, it does not test why polysemanticity arises or whether it occurs without capacity pressure.

Tests semantic matching for GPT2-SMALL SAE directions and neurons using a small set of hand-selected searches and one text snippet; does not establish that features are sparse in general or measure their distribution across neurons in LLMs broadly.
Does not test feature completeness, stability across conditions or models, or whether SAE features are canonical units.
Uses one-dimensional SAE directions but does not test whether the underlying represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relationships.reason: Direction matches fall from 19 to 7 across layers 3–11, with no advantage over neurons at layers 8–9. The top 'red' direction was literal-token rather than conceptual, and synonym activation was weaker (r1, r3, r4, r24–r32).

source_check.reason: Concept matching depends on layer and search context: later-layer matches are weaker overall, layer 8 is below neurons and layer 9 ties them, and literal-token directions need contextual disambiguation. This qualifies dictionary recovery quality without establishing absence of V4.
